children: | FSE:M0LY) is pleased to provide an update on the potential €50 million equity financing previously announced on April 27 that may include the European Innovation Council’s EIC STEP program and an industry investor. The EIC Fund’s due diligence process is progressing and in parallel, negotiations are ongoing with the parties involved. As previously announced, the Company has already completed the program’s initial stages: the eligibility assessment, including receipt of the Sovereignty STEP Seal for project excellence, and the panel of jurors’ recommendation about a potential investment by EIC Fund.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261028238125/en/
The financing remains subject to the EIC Fund’s final decision and the settlement of definitive documentation with other parties. The Company will provide further updates as appropriate.

Greenland Resources is a publicly listed Canadian and Greenlandic company developing Malmbjerg, a world-class Climax-type primary molybdenum deposit near tidewater in east-central Greenland. The project has a NI 43-101 Definitive Feasibility Study produced by Tetra Tech, a 30-year molybdenum and magnesium exploitation licence, an environmentally responsible mine design, and binding long term offtake agreements with major EU steel producers. Proven and probable reserves total 245 million tonnes grading 0.176% MoS2, containing 571 million pounds of molybdenum. As the high-grade molybdenum is mined for the first half of the mine life, the average annual production for years one to ten is 32.8 million pounds per year of contained molybdenum metal at an average grade of 0.23% MoS2, approximately 25% of EU total yearly consumption and 100% of EU defence needs. The Company received a grant from the government of Canada and is aiming to incorporate magnesium and rare earth elements as byproducts in the feasibility study. For more information, visit www.greenlandresources.ca or view the Company’s Canadian regulatory filings at www.sedarplus.com.
On December 3, 2025 the European Commission presented RESourceEU, and mentioned the Company’s Malmbjerg project in Greenland as a priority EU project.
